message.content:
Building a new PC can be a rewarding project, giving you a machine tailored to your needs and a deeper understanding of how it all works. Below is a comprehensive, step‑by‑step guide that covers everything from planning to troubleshooting.

---

## 1. Planning & Budgeting

| Item | What to consider | Typical price range |
|------|------------------|---------------------|
| **Use case** | Gaming, content creation, office work, general use | – |
| **Budget** | Total cost you’re willing to spend | $300–$2000+ |
| **Future‑proofing** | Will you upgrade components later? | – |
| **Form factor** | Full‑tower, mid‑tower, mini‑ITX | – |

### Quick Decision Matrix

| Use case | Recommended budget | Key component focus |
|----------|--------------------|---------------------|
| Office / browsing | <$400 | CPU, SSD |
| Light gaming | $400–$700 | GPU, PSU |
| Mid‑range gaming | $700–$1200 | GPU, CPU, RAM |
| High‑end gaming / streaming | $1200–$2000 | GPU, CPU, RAM, cooling |
| Content creation | $1000–$2500 | CPU, GPU, RAM, storage |

---

## 2. Component Selection

| Component | What to look for | Example models |
|-----------|------------------|----------------|
| **CPU** | Core count, clock speed, socket compatibility | AMD Ryzen 5 7600X, Intel Core i5‑13600K |
| **Motherboard** | Socket, chipset, form factor, expansion slots | ASUS TUF Gaming B650‑PLUS, MSI MPG Z790 CARBON |
| **RAM** | Capacity, speed, dual‑channel support | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16GB DDR5‑6000 |
| **GPU** | VRAM, memory bandwidth, power draw | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti, AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT |
| **Storage** | NVMe SSD for OS + SATA SSD/HDD for bulk | Samsung 980 PRO 1TB NVMe, WD Blue 2TB HDD |
| **PSU** | Wattage, efficiency rating (80+ Gold/Platinum), modularity | Seasonic Focus GX-750, Corsair RM850x |
| **Case** | Size, airflow, cable management | NZXT H510, Fractal Design Meshify C |
| **Cooling** | Air cooler vs. AIO liquid, noise level | Noctua NH-U12S, Corsair iCUE H100i |
| **Peripherals** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, headset | LG 27GL850, Logitech G502 HERO, HyperX Cloud II |

### Compatibility Checklist

1. **CPU ↔ Motherboard** – Verify socket type and BIOS support.
2. **Motherboard ↔ RAM** – Check supported DDR version and speeds.
3. **Motherboard ↔ GPU** – Ensure PCIe slot width (x16) and length clearance.
4. **Case ↔ GPU** – Measure GPU length vs. case clearance.
5. **Case ↔ PSU** – Confirm PSU form factor (ATX) and cable lengths.
6. **Case ↔ Cooling** – Verify fan mounting points and radiator clearance.

---

## 3. Tools & Workspace

| Tool | Why it’s useful |
|------|-----------------|
| **Phillips #2 screwdriver** | Most screws on boards and cases |
| **Anti‑static wrist strap** | Prevents electrostatic discharge (ESD) |
| **Cable ties / Velcro straps** | Keeps cables tidy |
| **Thermal paste** | Improves CPU‑cooler heat transfer |
| **Flash drive** | For BIOS updates or OS installation |
| **LED light** | Illuminates tight spaces |
| **Notebook / phone** | For quick reference or photos |

Set up a clean, flat surface with good lighting. Keep components on a non‑conductive mat or cardboard.

---

## 4. Step‑by‑Step Assembly

### 4.1 Prepare the Case

1. **Open the case** – Remove side panels.
2. **Install standoffs** – Screw into motherboard tray holes (match motherboard layout).
3. **Mount the PSU** – Align with rear exhaust, screw in place.
4. **Route cables** – Pull PSU cables through cable management holes.

### 4.2 Install the Motherboard

1. **Place the motherboard** – Align with standoffs and rear I/O shield.
2. **Secure it** – Tighten all screws evenly.
3. **Connect front panel headers** – Refer to motherboard manual for exact pinouts.

### 4.3 Install the CPU

1. **Open the CPU socket latch** – Lift lever.
2. **Align the CPU** – Match the triangle on the CPU with the socket.
3. **Drop the CPU gently** – Lower until it clicks.
4. **Close the latch** – Secure the CPU.

### 4.4 Apply Thermal Paste & Mount Cooler

1. **Clean the CPU surface** – Use isopropyl alcohol and lint‑free cloth.
2. **Apply paste** – Small pea‑size dot in the center.
3. **Mount the cooler** – Align with mounting holes, tighten in a cross pattern.
4. **Attach fan cables** – Connect to CPU fan header.

### 4.5 Install RAM

1. **Open RAM slots** – Push levers outward.
2. **Align RAM sticks** – Match notch with slot.
3. **Insert firmly** – Push until levers click back.

### 4.6 Install Storage

| NVMe SSD | SATA SSD/HDD |
|----------|--------------|
| 1. **Locate M.2 slot** – Usually near CPU. | 1. **Open SATA drive bay** – Slide in drive. |
| 2. **Insert SSD at 30° angle** – Align key. | 2. **Secure with screw** – Tighten. |
| 3. **Screw down** – Use provided screw. | 3. **Connect SATA data cable** – Plug into motherboard. |
| 4. **Connect SATA power cable** – From PSU. | 4. **Connect SATA power cable** – From PSU. |

### 4.7 Install GPU

1. **Remove expansion slot covers** – From rear of case.
2. **Insert GPU into PCIe x16 slot** – Align with slot and tray.
3. **Secure GPU** – Tighten screws to case.
4. **Connect power cables** – 8‑pin or 6‑pin from PSU to GPU.

### 4.8 Connect Power

| Cable | Connection |
|-------|------------|
| **24‑pin ATX** | Motherboard |
| **8‑pin EPS** | Motherboard (CPU) |
| **PCIe 8‑pin** | GPU |
| **SATA power** | SSD/HDD |
| **M.2 power** | NVMe SSD (if required) |
| **Front panel** | Case (power button, reset, LEDs) |

### 4.9 Cable Management

1. **Tidy cables** – Use ties or Velcro straps.
2. **Route cables behind motherboard tray** – Keeps airflow unobstructed.
3. **Check cable lengths** – Avoid excess slack that could block fans.

### 4.10 Final Checks

- **Double‑check all connections** – Power, data, front panel.
- **Verify cable routing** – No obstruction to fans.
- **Close side panels** – Secure screws.

---

## 5. First Boot & BIOS Setup

1. **Power on** – Press the case power button.
2. **Enter BIOS** – Press `Delete` or `F2` during POST.
3. **Set boot priority** – SSD first, then USB/DVD.
4. **Enable XMP** – For RAM overclocking (if applicable).
5. **Save & exit** – `F10` or `Save & Exit`.

---

## 6. Operating System Installation

1. **Create bootable USB** – Use Rufus or BalenaEtcher with Windows ISO or Linux distro.
2. **Boot from USB** – Select USB in boot menu.
3. **Follow installer prompts** – Partition SSD, install OS.
4. **Install drivers** – GPU, chipset, Wi‑Fi.
5. **Update Windows** – Install latest patches.

---

## 7. Post‑Build Testing

| Test | Tool | What to look for |
|------|------|------------------|
| **Stress test** | Prime95 (CPU), FurMark (GPU) | No crashes, temperatures <80 °C |
| **Benchmark** | 3DMark, Cinebench R23 | Performance matches expectations |
| **Temperature monitoring** | HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner | Idle <40 °C, load <80 °C |
| **Fan speed** | BIOS or software | Fans spin correctly, no stalls |

---

## 8. Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| **No POST / no display** | Loose GPU, missing power cable, wrong BIOS settings | Re‑seat GPU, check cables, reset BIOS |
| **System freezes during stress test** | Overheating, insufficient PSU | Improve airflow, upgrade PSU |
| **Blue screen of death (BSOD)** | Driver conflict, faulty RAM | Update drivers, run MemTest86 |
| **Fan not spinning** | Incorrect fan header, BIOS disabled | Connect to correct header, enable in BIOS |
| **USB ports not working** | BIOS setting, faulty USB controller | Enable in BIOS, update chipset drivers |

---

## 9. Maintenance Tips

- **Dust cleaning** – Every 3–6 months, use compressed air.
- **Thermal paste replacement** – Every 2–3 years or if temperatures rise.
- **Firmware updates** – Keep BIOS, GPU firmware up to date.
- **Cable reorganization** – When upgrading components, keep cables tidy.

---

## 10. Resources & Further Reading

| Resource | Type | Link |
|----------|------|------|
| **PCPartPicker** | Component compatibility checker | https://pcpartpicker.com |
| **Tom’s Hardware** | Reviews & guides | https://www.tomshardware.com |
| **Reddit r/buildapc** | Community support | https://www.reddit.com/r/buildapc |
| **YouTube channels** | Build walkthroughs | Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents |
| **Manufacturer manuals** | Detailed specs | Visit each component’s website |

---

### Quick Checklist (Before You Start)

- [ ] All components purchased & received.
- [ ] Anti‑static wrist strap ready.
- [ ] Case opened, standoffs installed.
- [ ] PSU cables routed.
- [ ] Motherboard mounted.
- [ ] CPU seated & cooler installed.
- [ ] RAM installed.
- [ ] Storage installed.
- [ ] GPU installed.
- [ ] All cables connected.
- [ ] BIOS set to boot from SSD.
- [ ] OS installed & drivers updated.

---

**Congratulations!** You’ve built a custom PC. Enjoy your new machine, and feel free to tweak settings or upgrade components as your needs evolve. Happy computing!
